To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the annual reports of the VSE firms in our sample only give little and unspecific information on the PPP activities and that the reporting of PPP activities is not a standard practice of firms in the VSE.
the annual reports of the investigated sample of firms listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange in 2005 only provide unspecific information about PPP activities.
firms report on PPP engagement to signal PPP activities beyond legal reporting obligations and that firms use the annual report to signal PPP activities in a qualitative way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether firms use annual reports to signal PPP activities to the public.
the disclosure of PPP projects in the annual reports.
the question if and to what extent firms report on PPP activities in annual reports and if so, how they do it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the annual reports of the examined firms do not signal PPP engagement.
firms do not report on PPP projects to signal PPP involvement to the capital market.
the firms’ annual reports do not reveal information on PPP activities to signal PPP engagement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reporting behavior of the sample’s companies is not consistent.
annual reports do not serve as a signaling tool in the PPP context.
firms do not signal PPP engagement in a systematic way, but rather use the annual report to communicate information that is not covered by the legal reporting requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lack of a PPP definition and of reporting obligations leads to the absence of PPP reporting in annual reports.
firms do not seem to use their annual reports to signal PPP activities, even though they have the chance to do so.
the lack of PPP information policy in annual reports is a result of the lack of a standardized PPP concept in France.
